payload.message:
JIRA sprint task allocation. Each agent chooses at most one micro-task (or skips). Maximize tasks completed, prefer higher-priority tasks, then minimize total cost. Avoid duplicate task selections and infeasible assignments.

NOTE: If environment.assignment_filling=true and an agent fails to assign a variable, the environment will fill any remaining unassigned variables with a uniform-random allowed assignment when producing final results.

This blackboard is a private communication channel.
Participants: Emil, Frida, Hipolito, Lamont, Lawanna, Raymond

payload.content: Lawanna planning: I have strong fit only on ISSUE-0001 ui-ux-design tasks with low costs: review/docs/triage each 1.09, test 1.52, implement 2.17. ISSUE-0002 tasks are prohibitively expensive (40/56/80), so I will avoid them. Tentative preference if uncontested: ISSUE-0001::review, otherwise docs or triage as backups. Please share your intended claims so we can avoid duplicates and maximize coverage.

Emil planning (iter 1): availability 9h; strongest fits are data-science 0.84 and ui-ux-design 0.68. My private costs: ISSUE-0001 review/docs/triage 1.28 each, test 1.79, implement 2.56; ISSUE-0002 review 7.73, test 10.82, implement 15.45. To maximize tasks completed and avoid duplicates, I prefer taking an unclaimed low-cost ISSUE-0001 task rather than expensive ISSUE-0002. Since Lawanna tentatively prefers ISSUE-0001::review, my tentative ranking is ISSUE-0001::docs or ISSUE-0001::triage first, then ISSUE-0001::test, then ISSUE-0001::implement; I will avoid review if Lawanna keeps it. If others have much better fit/cost on remaining ISSUE-0001 tasks, I can adapt, but currently planning to reserve docs/triage.

Raymond planning (iter 1): availability 9h; strongest fits data-science 0.86 and documentation 0.81. My private costs strongly favor ISSUE-0002 data-science/documentation tasks: review 4.29, test 6.01, implement 8.59. ISSUE-0001 ui-ux-design tasks are very expensive for me (review/docs/triage 10, test 14, implement 20), so I should avoid ISSUE-0001 unless absolutely necessary. Tentative preference is ISSUE-0002::review as best value, with ISSUE-0002::test backup, then implement. Given Lawanna/Emil are both efficient on ISSUE-0001, I recommend they cover distinct ISSUE-0001 micro-tasks while I target ISSUE-0002::review to maximize completed tasks and minimize cost. Please share if anyone else has an even lower cost on ISSUE-0002::review so I can switch to test if needed. (phase=planning, iter=1)

Lamont planning (iter 1): availability 4h; strongest fits data-science 0.96 and documentation 0.82. My private costs favor ISSUE-0002::review at 4.04; ISSUE-0002::test is 7.26 and likely infeasible given 5.6h effort > 4h availability; ISSUE-0002::implement is 12.08 and also infeasible at 8h. ISSUE-0001 ui-ux-design tasks are all expensive for me (review/docs/triage 10, test 14, implement 20), so I should avoid ISSUE-0001. I currently tentatively prefer ISSUE-0002::review if uncontested; if Raymond has stronger claim there, I can likely skip rather than take a high-cost or infeasible task. Please share if anyone else can cover ISSUE-0002::test/implement efficiently while Raymond or I take review.

Frida planning (iter 1): availability 4h; strongest fits ui-ux-design 0.94 and data-science 0.73. My private costs strongly favor ISSUE-0001 ui-ux-design tasks: review/docs/triage each 0.96, test 1.35, implement 1.93. ISSUE-0002 tasks are poor for me and mostly infeasible/very costly: review 8.56 (feasible but expensive), test 13.59 and implement 21.13 are infeasible by effort > availability. To maximize tasks completed and avoid duplicates, I should target an unclaimed ISSUE-0001 micro-task. Since Lawanna tentatively wants ISSUE-0001::review and Emil tentatively wants docs/triage, my tentative preference is ISSUE-0001::triage or ISSUE-0001::docs (whichever Emil does not take), with ISSUE-0001::test as next backup, and avoid ISSUE-0002 unless coordination requires. Also noting Raymond (4.29) is better than Lamont (4.04 slightly better actually) on ISSUE-0002::review, but only one of them should take it; the other may need to skip unless someone can cover another feasible task. I currently lean ISSUE-0001::triage if Emil takes docs.

Hipolito planning (iter 1): availability 5h; strongest fits documentation 0.78 and ui-ux-design 0.64. My private costs: ISSUE-0001 review/docs/triage each 1.36, test 1.90, implement 2.71; ISSUE-0002 review 8.18, test 12.05, implement 19.36. So I am efficient only on ISSUE-0001 and should avoid ISSUE-0002 due to high cost / infeasibility. Given current tentative claims: Lawanna->0001::review, Emil->0001::docs or triage, Frida->0001::triage or docs, Raymond/Lamont contest 0002::review. To maximize completed tasks and avoid duplicates, I tentatively propose taking ISSUE-0001::test (or ISSUE-0001::implement if test is needed elsewhere), since that leaves review/docs/triage for lower-cost specialists and gives us another distinct feasible high-priority micro-task. If others strongly prefer different coverage, I can adapt, but my current best unique slot is ISSUE-0001::test.

Lawanna update (planning iter 1): Based on current declarations, a low-cost non-duplicate coverage plan appears to be: Lawanna->ISSUE-0001::review (1.09), Emil->ISSUE-0001::docs (1.28), Frida->ISSUE-0001::triage (0.96), Hipolito->ISSUE-0001::test (1.90), and then choose ONE of Raymond/Lamont for ISSUE-0002::review, preferably Lamont at 4.04 since slightly cheaper than Raymond 4.29; the other should likely skip unless another agent can cheaply cover ISSUE-0001::implement. I can also switch from review to docs/triage if needed, but review remains my best tentative slot. Suggest Raymond consider ISSUE-0002::test only if someone values tasks_done enough to justify cost 6.01 and feasibility; otherwise skip may be better depending on scoring weights. Please confirm intended final claims to lock a collision-free assignment set.

Emil update (planning iter 1): I support the emerging collision-free plan. Given current declarations and my costs, I tentatively commit to ISSUE-0001::docs, with ISSUE-0001::triage as backup only if Frida/Lawanna need docs and no one else covers triage. Recommended set from my view: Lawanna->0001::review, Emil->0001::docs, Frida->0001::triage, Hipolito->0001::test, Lamont->0002::review (slightly cheaper than Raymond), Raymond->skip unless he has a compelling reason to take 0002::test under scoring weights. This yields 5 distinct feasible high-priority tasks at relatively low total cost and leaves only 0001::implement and expensive 0002 tasks uncovered. Unless objections arise, I plan to keep docs in execution.

Raymond update (planning iter 1): I agree with the emerging low-cost collision-free allocation. Since Lamont is slightly cheaper than me on ISSUE-0002::review (4.04 vs 4.29) and I am the next-best feasible option on ISSUE-0002::test at cost 6.01, my current recommendation is: Lawanna->ISSUE-0001::review, Emil->ISSUE-0001::docs, Frida->ISSUE-0001::triage, Hipolito->ISSUE-0001::test, Lamont->ISSUE-0002::review, and I tentatively SKIP in execution unless someone drops out or unless we decide the extra feasible task ISSUE-0002::test is worth its added cost under scoring. If any agent cannot commit their tentative task, I can backfill ISSUE-0002::review or ISSUE-0002::test as needed, but to avoid duplicates my current plan is skip.

Lamont update (planning iter 1): I support the current collision-free allocation and will tentatively reserve ISSUE-0002::review for execution. My feasible/low-cost set remains only ISSUE-0002::review at 4.04; ISSUE-0002::test and implement are infeasible by effort relative to my 4h availability, and ISSUE-0001 tasks are much higher cost for me. So my intended final claim is ISSUE-0002::review unless coordination changes. Recommended set still looks strongest as Lawanna->0001::review, Emil->0001::docs, Frida->0001::triage, Hipolito->0001::test, Lamont->0002::review, Raymond->skip/backfill only if someone drops. (phase=planning, iter=1)
